By late afternoon on 14 September 2024, the final day of the Eddlestone Dog Trials, the showground had settled into the hush that follows a long contest. Handlers sat on hay bales, their dogs sprawled at their feet, while the last rosettes were laid out on a trestle table beside the ring.

The trials have been a fixture of the district for generations, a gathering where working instinct is measured against patient training. This year 212 dogs across 31 breeds competed, the kind of breadth that once seemed unthinkable for so local an event.

After the closing ceremony, Marguerite Holloway, chief steward of the Eddlestone Canine Association, announced the result: a border collie had taken best in show. The association's official results bulletin, issued afterward, confirmed it.

It was, many in the crowd remarked, a fitting winner for a place built on herding country.
